tools.name: get_company_overview
tools.description: Get a structured overview of Flamel: what the product does, who it is for, the solution areas, key links, and how to contact sales or start a trial. Start here if you know nothing about Flamel.

tools.name: search_flamel_content
tools.description: Full-text search across Flamel's published blog posts, case studies, and FAQ entries. Use this first when you do not already know which page answers the question.

tools.name: list_blog_posts
tools.description: List published Flamel blog posts, newest first. Optionally filter by category. Returns titles, URLs, summaries, and publish dates, not full bodies.

tools.name: get_blog_post
tools.description: Fetch the full body of one published Flamel blog post as Markdown, by slug.

tools.name: list_blog_categories
tools.description: List the blog categories available for filtering `list_blog_posts`.

tools.name: list_case_studies
tools.description: List published Flamel customer case studies with their headline results.

tools.name: get_case_study
tools.description: Fetch one Flamel case study by slug: the challenge, the solution, the results, and customer quotes.

tools.name: list_faqs
tools.description: List published Flamel FAQ entries: platform capabilities, pricing model, onboarding, integrations, and security. Good for direct factual questions about the product.

tools.name: list_testimonials
tools.description: List published customer testimonials about Flamel, with the author name, title, and company.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_flamel_content, list_blog_posts, get_blog_post · Private data: get_company_overview · Public sink: list_blog_posts, get_blog_post.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_flamel_content, list_blog_posts, get_blog_post · Private data: get_company_overview · Public sink: list_blog_posts, get_blog_post

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
